questions.explanation:
The Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scales have represented the traditional gold standard in intellectual assessment for many years, based on carefully developed normative standards.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a type of validity?
questions.explanation:
Inter-rater reliability (not validity) is a measure of agreement between two or more observers evaluating the same subjects using the same information.

questions.question_text: Which of the following rating scales for depression used in adults is well validated in children aged 14 and older?
questions.explanation:
The Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) was developed in the early 1960s to rate depression severity, with a focus on behavioural and cognitive dimensions of depression. It is a self-rated questionnaire containing 21 statements, with four possible responses for each. The current version has added more coverage of somatic symptoms and covers the most recent 2 weeks. Because it is a self-report measure, it can be used to screen for major depression (in individuals aged 13 and older). A score of >17 indicates moderate and >30 indicates severe depression.
Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 39.

The Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) was developed in the late 1960s as a short clinician-rated scale (based on observation) for measuring the severity of psychiatric symptomatology. It consists of 18 or 24 items, each rated on a 7-8 point scale. correct_answers.text: It includes most of the components of cognition that are commonly affected by dementia

questions.question_text: What is the most reliable instrument to make a clinical diagnosis according to DSM criteria?
questions.explanation:
The Structured Clinical Interview for the DSM (SCID) is one of the most used diagnostic instruments in clinical research worldwide. The latest version of the instrument is called ‘SCID-5’. SCID is a clinician-administered semi-structured interview for use in patients in whom a psychiatric diagnosis is suspected. It is primarily used in research with trained interviewers.
Ref: Osório FL et al. Clinical validity and intrarater and test–retest reliability of the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM‐5–Clinician Version (SCID‐5‐CV). Psychiatry and clinical neurosciences. 2019 Dec;73(12):754-60.

questions.question_text: With respect to Young Mania Rating Scale, which of the following is least likely to be correct?

options.text: It does not have items on suicidality
Psychotic symptoms are not included in the scale

questions.explanation:
The Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS) has 11 items and is based on the patient’s subjective report of their condition over the previous 48 hours. Additional information is based upon clinical observations made during the course of the clinical interview. There are four items that are graded on a scale from 0 to 8 (irritability, speech, thought content, and disruptive/aggressive behaviour), while the remaining seven items are graded on a scale of 0 to 4. Mania is indicated by a score of 12, but many clinical studies require YMRS > 20 to determine a manic state.
Ref: Di Giacomo E et al. Unblending borderline personality and bipolar disorders. Journal of psychiatric research. 2017 Aug 1;91:90-7.

questions.question_text: Which is the most commonly used screening tool to diagnose dementia in older people?
questions.explanation: MMSE: Cut off 24/30, takes 5-10 minutes to complete and is a standard baseline test. It is the most widely used cognitive test in old age psychiatry and has been validated in a variety of populations. It is good for screening global cognitive dysfunctions as opposed to focal cognitive dysfunctions. It covers the following areas of cognition such as orientation, memory, concentration, language, praxis and Gnosis

questions.question_text: Which of the following interview schedules have replaced the Present Status Examination in contemporary epidemiological studies?
questions.explanation:
The Schedules for Clinical Assessment in Neuropsychiatry (SCAN) has evolved from the older Present State Examination (PSE). SCAN is a set of instruments aimed at assessing and classifying psychopathology in adults. Instruments include the PSE-10 (the tenth edition of the Present State Examination), the SCAN glossary, the Item Group Checklist, and the Clinical History Schedule. The interview is semi-structured, the aim being to encapsulate the clinical interview while minimising its vagaries. Where there is doubt, the interviewer can proceed to a freestyle interview to clarify further. It is designed for use by psychiatrists or clinical psychologists, thereby utilising clinical interviewing skills in evaluating each symptom. The use of mental health professionals in interviewing with SCAN makes this an expensive method but has the advantage of approximating the ‘gold standard’ diagnosis achieved by clinical interview.
Ref: Casey P, Kelly B. Fish’s clinical pathology: Signs and symptoms in psychiatry, 4th Edition. 2019.p. 9.
